He used to commit one theft a year on average. The stolen money lasted for the year. B. He chose the house at Shotover Grange to commit his next burglary. He studied the design of the house carefully for a fortnight. C. He found that the family had gone to London and the servants to the movie. He broke into the house one afternoon. D. He hoped to get fifteen thousand pounds worth of jewels from the safe.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. He used to commit one theft a year on average. The stolen money lasted for the year.

B. He chose the house at Shotover Grange to commit his next burglary. He studied the design of the house carefully for a fortnight.

C. He found that the family had gone to London and the servants to the movie. He broke into the house one afternoon.

D. He hoped to get fifteen thousand pounds worth of jewels from the safe.
questions.solution: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is 'ABCD'. Sentence A comes first as it establishes the background information about the thief's modus operandi, indicating that he commits one theft per year on average, and the stolen money sustains him throughout the year. Sentence B follows logically after Sentence A because it describes the thief's planning process for his next burglary. Since he commits one theft per year, he carefully selects the house at Shotover Grange for his next crime and spends a fortnight studying its design. Sentence C logically follows Sentence B because it describes the thief's action of breaking into the house at Shotover Grange. After carefully planning his burglary, he takes advantage of the opportune moment when he discovers that the family is away and the servants are occupied elsewhere. Finally, Sentence D logically follows Sentence C because it reveals the thief's motive for breaking into the house - to steal jewels worth fifteen thousand pounds from the safe. This sentence provides insight into the specific target of the theft. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.solution: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is BDCA. Sentence B comes first as it establishes the context by explaining how the drop in the death rate has contributed to the rapid rise in population. Sentence D logically follows Sentence B because it provides specific data to support the claim made in Sentence B. By mentioning the death rate in India in 2001, it offers concrete evidence of the phenomenon discussed. Sentence C logically follows Sentence D because it explains the reason behind the decrease in the death rate mentioned in Sentence D. It introduces the concept of medical breakthroughs as a factor contributing to the decline in mortality rates. Finally, Sentence A logically follows Sentence C because it elaborates on the positive consequences of medical breakthroughs mentioned in Sentence C. By mentioning that chronic infections are no longer feared, it illustrates one of the tangible benefits of medical advancements and the decrease in mortality rates. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. There are 1.52 billion Aadhaar cards given to the whole population as of February 2019.

B. A financial inclusion programme called the Prime Minister's Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) makes services like banking, remittance, and insurance accessible to every Indian at a reasonable price.

C. Under the acronym JAM - Jan Dhan Yojana for Financial Inclusion, Aadhaar Biometric Identification, and Mobile Telecommunications - India is on the verge of a social revolution.

D. Beneficiaries may open an account with no balance.
questions.solution: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is CABD. Sentence C introduces the concept of the JAM acronym, which stands for Jan Dhan Yojana for Financial Inclusion, Aadhaar Biometric Identification, and Mobile Telecommunications. This sets the stage for discussing various government initiatives aimed at social revolution and transformation. Sentence A logically follows Sentence C because it provides specific data about one of the components of the JAM acronym, namely Aadhaar Biometric Identification. By mentioning the number of Aadhaar cards issued to the entire population as of February 2019, it demonstrates the widespread adoption and implementation of this biometric identification system. Sentence B introduces the Prime Minister's Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), which is a financial inclusion program. This sentence explains how the PMJDY aims to make banking, remittance, and insurance services accessible to every Indian at affordable prices. Finally, Sentence D logically follows Sentence B because it provides additional information about the Prime Minister's Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), specifically mentioning that beneficiaries can open accounts with no balance (Accordingly, BD forms a necessary pair). This highlights a key feature of the financial inclusion program, emphasising its inclusivity and accessibility to even those with limited financial resources. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.solution: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is BADC. Sentence B introduces the historical context by stating that locusts have caused plagues since prehistoric times. This sets the stage for discussing the impact and control of locust swarms throughout history. Sentence A logically follows Sentence B because it elaborates on the consequence of locust swarms mentioned in the historical context (Accordingly, BA forms a necessary pair). It explains how swarms have wreaked havoc on crops and caused famines and mass migrations. This sentence provides specific examples of the devastating effects of locust plagues. Sentence D introduces recent advancements in controlling locust swarms. It discusses changes in agricultural practices and improved observation methods that have allowed control measures to be implemented earlier. This sentence suggests progress in addressing the issue of locust infestations. Finally, Sentence C logically follows Sentence D because it elaborates on the methods of controlling locust swarms mentioned in the previous sentence (Accordingly, DC forms a necessary pair). It discusses traditional methods, such as pesticide use, as well as emerging approaches like biological control, highlighting the ongoing efforts to combat locust infestations. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Meenakshi sweeps the ball excellently when she _____ an off-spin delivery.

Meenakshi sweeps the ball excellently when she _____ an off-spin delivery.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'gets'. This option is correct because it is in the simple present tense, which is commonly used to express habitual actions or general truths. In the given context, "gets" indicates the action of Meenakshi sweeping the ball excellently as a response to an off-spin delivery.

Option (a) uses the future tense ("will get"), which suggests that the action of sweeping the ball excellently will occur in the future. But the sentence describes a habitual or general action that Meenakshi performs when faced with an off-spin delivery. The simple present tense is more appropriate for expressing habitual actions or general truths.

Option (b) uses the present perfect tense ("has got"), which indicates an action that started in the past and has relevance to the present moment. The present perfect tense is not suitable in the given context because the sentence does not emphasise the completion of the action, but rather the habit of sweeping the ball excellently in response to an off-spin delivery.

Option (c) uses the simple past tense ("got"), which indicates an action that occurred in the past. But the sentence does not describe a specific past event. Accordingly, this option is incorrect. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: An experiment is being studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.
